note: PM check: Week 1 still hasn't kicked off (tonight's Niners-Rams opener in Melbourne is the first game; everything else is Sunday/Monday) and all ten rosters still show $0 FAAB used, so pricing is still band-based, not bid-history. Michael Mayer is now off the board (rostered by Stipe since the morning check) and drops out of the target list below. Chris Rodriguez and Tre Tucker remain unclaimed and their cases are unchanged. New this check: Seahawks QB Sam Darnold (hip) is expected to miss Week 2 with Drew Lock starting in relief — noted below as a pass for this roster.

targets.why: Jacksonville's initial depth chart lists Rodriguez and your own Bhayshul Tuten as RB co-starters, with OC Grant Udinski framing it as a real '1A/1B' hot-hand combo rather than naming a lead back (Yahoo Sports, Sept. 10). Tuten also sat out a practice this week with an illness, and Rodriguez has 33 career carries inside the 20 for short-yardage/goal-line work.
targets.asset: The other half of a genuine committee backfield you already own one side of — projected as a real 8-12 touch role with goal-line upside if Tuten's illness lingers or the committee tilts his way on a given week.
targets.my_team_impact: Doesn't start over Tuten, but this is direct insurance on a roster asset you're already relying on: if Rodriguez's half of the committee grows (or Tuten misses time), you'd rather hold both halves than let a rival scoop the other one. Cheap to roster given the shared bench-worthiness.
targets.confidence_why: Coach language and camp/practice reporting confirm a real committee, but neither back has taken an NFL snap in it yet — role could still tilt hard either direction once games start.
targets.competition: No rival roster shows a Jaguars-backfield stake or an acute RB hole from this week's news; unclaimed since at least last check.
targets.bid: 3 dollars — routine-uncontested band, no rival interest signaled
targets.drop: Kayshon Boutte — just traded to Houston with limited practice reps, expected light Week 1 snaps behind more tenured Texans WRs.

targets.why: Brock Bowers (meniscus trim) is out 'a game or two,' vacating roughly 30% of the Raiders' target share; multiple outlets (SI onsi, FantasyPros, Sept. 9-10) project Tucker as the single biggest beneficiary at close to a 25% share for as long as Bowers sits.
targets.asset: Established, healthy Raiders WR1-by-default for 1-2 weeks in a Kirk Cousins-led veteran passing game, not a camp battle unknown.
targets.my_team_impact: Would be a clean upgrade over Quentin Johnston or Kayshon Boutte as a streaming half-PPR FLEX for however long Bowers is out, but it's a rental — the bump fades the moment Bowers returns, and you can only make one bench move this week without cutting deeper into your own WR depth.
targets.confidence_why: Pure target-share math off a vacancy, not a live snap sample — treat as a short two-week window, not a role change.
targets.competition: Nationally hyped as a Week 1 waiver-wire target, so expect contested league-wide interest even though no hbgbs rival has a specific WR hole flagged this week.
targets.bid: 5 dollars — worth a modest claim only if you pass on Rodriguez; not worth bidding both up against your own bench limit
targets.drop: Quentin Johnston — the better bench hold of your two WR depth pieces (named a Week 1 starter on LAC's own depth chart), so use Boutte for this claim instead if both are live.

targets.why: Sam Darnold left Wednesday's (Sept. 9) opener with a hip injury and is expected to miss Week 2 at Arizona; Lock relieved him and finished the win (187 yards, a TD, one sack, no turnovers) and is now Seattle's starter until Darnold returns.
targets.asset: A one-week (maybe two) streaming starter in a passing offense that just showed it can move the ball with him under center.
targets.rate_basis: one live relief appearance (Sept. 9), no starts yet
targets.my_team_impact: No fit — Justin Herbert is a locked, healthy starter with no bye this early, so Lock wouldn't crack your lineup even as a stash; this format's thin QB depth doesn't change that when your QB1 is already secure.
targets.confidence_why: Team-fit read, not a player-value one — your own QB spot is settled regardless of Lock's role in Seattle.
targets.competition: Unrostered league-wide as of this check; nobody in the HBGBs has a QB hole this news would fill.
